venues.name: SCAI The Bathhouse
venues.about: SCAI The Bathhouse is a contemporary art gallery in Yanaka, Tokyo, housed in a converted 200-year-old public bathhouse near Ueno's museum district. Established in 1993 (the gallery also cites 1989 elsewhere), it has built the careers of major postwar Japanese artists associated with the Mono-ha movement, as well as figures such as Toshikatsu Endo and Mariko Mori, while promoting younger talents like Kohei Nawa and Reijiro Wada. International artists including Anish Kapoor, Darren Almond, Apichatpong Weerasethakul, and He Xiangyu have created works in dialogue with Japanese culture through the gallery. SCAI has also organized public art projects in Tokyo, including installations at Roppongi Hills, and operates additional spaces—SCAI PARK in Tennozu Isle and SCAI PIRAMIDE in Roppongi—extending its program of exhibitions, preservation, and experimental projects for emerging artists.

venues.name: Ota Fine Arts
venues.about: Ota Fine Arts was founded in 1994 in Tokyo, initially in the Ebisu area, and has long positioned itself as a pioneer of Japanese contemporary art, notably giving early support to Yayoi Kusama. The gallery moved to Roppongi in 2003, relocated to the Tokyo bay area, and returned to a renewed Roppongi space in 2011. It later opened a nearby viewing room, 7CHOME, near the National Art Center. The gallery expanded internationally with a Singapore space at Gillman Barracks in 2012 and a Shanghai gallery in 2017, which reopened in the Rockbund district in 2023. Ota Fine Arts represents artists working in painting, video, craft and installation, with a program emphasizing dialogue among East and Southeast Asian, and more recently Middle Eastern, artists.

venues.name: ShugoArts
venues.about: ShugoArts is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Roppongi district, founded in 2000 by Shugo Satani, who drew on experience gained at his father Kazuhiko's Satani Gallery. Working with a deliberately small roster, the gallery builds long-term relationships with each artist, staging exhibitions that let their practices develop over time. Its program spans generations, from painters and sculptors who rose to prominence in the 1980s to photographers and artists who emerged from the 2000s onward, encompassing painting, sculpture, photography and glass work. In recent years ShugoArts has also dealt in secondary-market twentieth-century masterpieces, contributing to museum and private collection-building in Japan and abroad.

venues.name: Tomio Koyama Gallery
venues.about: Tomio Koyama Gallery is a Tokyo contemporary art gallery founded in 1996 in Saga-cho, Koto-ku, by Tomio Koyama. It has since expanded to multiple spaces across the city, currently operating in Roppongi, Tennoz and Kyobashi (opened 2024), as well as a space in Maebashi. Since its founding the gallery has been active on the international art fair circuit and has served as an early platform for young Japanese artists, helping to shape a current within Japanese contemporary art. It represents artists including Kishio Suga, Mika Ninagawa, Hiroshi Sugito and Richard Tuttle, alongside ceramic artists, and presents a program spanning established and emerging talents across nationalities and media.

venues.name: Mizuma Art Gallery
venues.about: Mizuma Art Gallery was founded in Tokyo in 1994 by executive director Mizuma Sueo. The gallery introduces Japanese and Asian artists with distinctive, style-independent sensibilities to the international art scene. As contemporary art markets in Asia expanded, Mizuma opened a Beijing space in 2008 and a Singapore gallery at Gillman Barracks in 2012, followed by an artist residence, Rumah Kijang Mizuma, in Yogyakarta in 2014 to foster exchange between Japanese and Indonesian artists. The gallery is known for active participation in major international fairs such as Art Basel Hong Kong and The Armory Show, and for producing artists who have gone on to international careers.

venues.name: Perrotin Tokyo
venues.about: Perrotin is an international contemporary art gallery founded in Paris in 1990 by Emmanuel Perrotin, then twenty-one years old. Over three decades the gallery has grown from a single Paris space into a network of more than twenty locations across Europe, Asia, and North America, including a gallery in Tokyo's Roppongi district. Perrotin's program is deliberately eclectic, spanning painting, sculpture, photography, and new media, and bringing together established figures, artists represented for decades, younger emerging talents, and several artist estates. The gallery describes its roster as spanning around eighteen nationalities and four continents, reflecting a stated commitment to diversity of generation, background, and medium rather than adherence to a single movement or aesthetic.

venues.name: Pace Tokyo
venues.about: Pace Gallery is a global contemporary art gallery founded in Boston in 1960 by Arne Glimcher, now led by CEO Marc Glimcher and President Samanthe Rubell. Working with roughly eighty artists and several estates, Pace's program pairs emerging and established contemporary figures with twentieth-century forebears, spanning painting, sculpture, photography, and light-based installation. The gallery operates spaces in New York, Los Angeles, London, Geneva, Berlin, Seoul, and Tokyo, with offices in Beijing and Hong Kong. Its Tokyo location, in the Azabudai Hills development, presents exhibitions by artists including Nigel Cooke and forms part of Pace's growing presence across Asia.

venues.name: Take Ninagawa
venues.about: Take Ninagawa is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Minato City, founded in 2008 by Atsuko Ninagawa. Since opening, it has operated from its Higashi Azabu address. The gallery represents a diverse group of Japanese and international artists working across painting, sculpture, video, and installation, spanning generations from postwar figures to emerging practitioners. It has participated in international art fairs including Art Basel Hong Kong, NADA, and FIAC Paris, and was a founding member of the New Tokyo Contemporaries association, reflecting its role in Tokyo's contemporary gallery scene.

venues.name: Kaikai Kiki Gallery
venues.about: Kaikai Kiki Gallery occupies the basement of an office building in Motoazabu, Tokyo, that once served as the private viewing room for Kaikai Kiki's headquarters. The space was reopened as a public gallery in March 2008, after Kaikai Kiki relocated from a prefab studio in Saitama's Asaka city to Tokyo in 2006. The gallery presents exhibitions of its own roster of Kaikai Kiki artists alongside international figures such as Mark Grotjahn, Matthew Monahan, Seonna Hong and Friedrich Kunath, aiming to build connections between Japanese and international contemporary art. Its stated goal is to manage artists and sell work in a way that gives art new social value, continuing to invite artists from both Japan and abroad to exhibit in its roughly 197 square meter exhibition space.

venues.name: NANZUKA
venues.about: NANZUKA is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo, founded by Shinji Nanzuka in 2005 in Shibuya as Nanzuka Underground, originally in a basement near Shibuya Crossing. The gallery focuses on rediscovering Japanese artists who were overlooked in the postwar fine-art scene, such as pop-art pioneer Keiichi Tanaami and airbrush illustrator Harumi Yamaguchi, while also promoting emerging Japanese talent and select international artists internationally. NANZUKA frequently collaborates with the fashion, music and design industries, expanding notions of what constitutes fine art. In 2021 it relocated its main space to a dedicated building in Harajuku and also runs satellite project spaces, Nanzuka 2G and 3110NZ. From 2013 to 2024 it operated a joint-venture branch in Hong Kong, AISHONANZUKA.

venues.name: Gallery Koyanagi
venues.about: Gallery Koyanagi is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Ginza district, occupying the ninth floor of the Koyanagi Building. It represents a roster of Japanese and international artists working across photography, sculpture, painting, video, and installation, including Hiroshi Sugimoto, Yoshihiro Suda, Christian Marclay, Marlene Dumas, and Tabaimo. The gallery's history is tied to Toho Koyanagi (Koyanagi Ceramics), a predecessor referenced in artist research on the space's Ginza site. Its program spans emerging and established artists, with regular solo and group exhibitions, museum collaborations, and participation in Art Week Tokyo. The gallery has also produced limited-edition publications and supported artists' museum surveys internationally, reflecting a program oriented toward serious, research-driven contemporary practice rather than purely market-driven display.

venues.name: Yutaka Kikutake Gallery
venues.about: Yutaka Kikutake Gallery opened in Roppongi, Tokyo, in 2015, later adding a second space in Kyobashi in 2024. The gallery presents exhibitions of international and domestic artists, supporting their practices and seeking opportunities to present their work internationally. Grounded in a strong sense of recent art history, the program explores newly created forms of expression and emphasizes art's contribution to society. Beyond exhibitions, the gallery runs workshops for all ages and publishes artist books alongside the lifestyle and culture magazine Chic and the art criticism journal Kyoku. The Kyobashi space focuses on group exhibitions reflecting the gallery's core values.

venues.name: Tokyo Gallery + BTAP
venues.about: Tokyo Gallery + BTAP is Japan's oldest contemporary art gallery, founded in Tokyo in 1950 by Yamamoto Takashi together with Shimizu Kusuo, initially as the Sukiyabashi Gallery. From the late 1950s it introduced Western abstraction, Gutai, Neo Dada and Mono-ha artists, later becoming a key champion of postwar Korean and Chinese contemporary art. In 2002 it opened BTAP in Beijing's 798 Art Zone, and in 2006 adopted its current dual name. Led today by Yamamoto Toyotsugu in Tokyo and Tabata Yukito in Beijing, the gallery continues to present postwar Japanese art alongside younger generations of artists across Japan, Korea and China, and takes part regularly in international art fairs.

venues.name: Kotaro Nukaga
venues.about: KOTARO NUKAGA is a contemporary art gallery founded in Tokyo in 2018 by director Kotaro Nukaga, who also runs the historic NUKAGA GALLERY. The gallery operates three spaces in Tokyo—two in the Tennoz district (Tennoz and Three) and one in Roppongi—positioning itself at the intersection of Japanese and international contemporary practice. Its program favors avant-garde and cross-disciplinary work, drawing on history, science and technology to question established art-world discourse. The gallery represents a mix of emerging and established Japanese and overseas artists, supporting their development through exhibitions, artist liaison services and participation in international art fairs, while aiming to expand the boundaries of conventional gallery programming.

venues.name: Maki Fine Arts
venues.about: Maki Fine Arts is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo, founded in the fall of 2010 by director Takahiro Maki. The gallery originally opened in Chuo-ku and relocated in 2015 to its current space in Kagurazaka, Shinjuku-ku. Its program represents a group of Japanese and international artists working across painting, sculpture, and mixed media, and the gallery regularly participates in art fairs in Japan and abroad, including NADA New York, Art Fair Tokyo, and Art Collaboration Kyoto. Represented artists have also been featured in institutional exhibitions at museums such as the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo and the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo.

venues.name: GALLERY MoMo Ryogoku
venues.about: GALLERY MoMo is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo, established in 2003 in Roppongi. In 2008 it opened a larger space in Ryogoku, and in 2013 the original Roppongi space was reopened as GALLERY MoMo Projects, focused on discovering young Japanese and international artists and curators. The gallery mainly represents Japanese artists born in the 1970s and 1980s, whose work reflects contemporary states of mind through personal styles, while also seeking connections to a global artistic context. Its stated mission is to introduce international artists with distinctive concepts to Japanese audiences, and to bring Japanese artists to audiences abroad.

venues.name: Kana Kawanishi Gallery
venues.about: Kana Kawanishi Gallery is a Tokyo contemporary art gallery led by director Kana Kawanishi, operating two exhibition spaces in the city: a gallery in Kiyosumi‑Shirakawa and a photography‑focused space, Kana Kawanishi Photography, in Nishi‑Azabu. The gallery represents a roster of mostly Japanese artists working across photography, painting, sculpture and mixed‑media installation, alongside a smaller group of international artists, including Finnish photographers. Its program mixes solo and group exhibitions with an active presence at international art fairs such as NADA New York, Frieze Seoul, Unseen Amsterdam, Photo London and Photo Basel, as well as Tokyo‑based fairs like Hibiya Okuroji and Art Fair Tokyo. The gallery also runs an affiliated art office handling publication, translation and editorial projects for artists and institutions.

venues.name: EUKARYOTE
venues.about: EUKARYOTE is a contemporary art gallery in Jingumae, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, established in 2018. Taking its name from the biological term for organisms whose cells contain a nucleus, the gallery frames its program around a recurring cycle of artistic evolution, likening it to the metabolism of living systems. It presents artists and artworks engaging with the tension between tangibility and intangibility in contemporary practice. Since opening, EUKARYOTE has regularly participated in art fairs across Japan and abroad, including ART OSAKA, Art Fair Asia Fukuoka, Art Collaboration Kyoto, and international fairs such as ART OnO Seoul, alongside group exhibitions and gallery-weekend events in Tokyo. The gallery represents a roster of primarily Japanese contemporary artists working across painting and other media.

venues.name: √K Contemporary
venues.about: √K Contemporary is a contemporary art gallery in the Kagurazaka district of Tokyo, opened in March 2020 by SEI-RIN Co., Ltd., the company behind the long-established Japanese art dealer Kashima Arts. Its 300-square-metre space was designed around an 'outer space' concept, intended to present works with new values and perspectives. The gallery focuses on introducing a new generation of Japanese and international artists working across painting, photography, sculpture and new media, while situating their work within the broader lineage of Japanese art history. Below the main gallery, Space √K offers an industrial concrete basement rentable for exhibitions, fashion shows, and performances. The gallery regularly participates in major regional art fairs and has been featured in international art press.

venues.name: GALLERY SIDE 2
venues.about: Gallery Side 2 is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Roppongi district, representing a small international roster of artists working across painting, sculpture, installation and photography. Its program brings together Japanese artists such as Jun Fujita, Takeo Hanazawa, Eikei Inamori, Shiko Sato and Masaru Tatsuki with Southeast Asian and Italian figures including Udomsak Krisanamis, Thaiwijit Puengkasemsomboon, Michelangelo Consani and the late Santi Alleruzzo, alongside internationally established names like Rirkrit Tiravanija, Peter McDonald and Jae Yong Rhee. The gallery has staged solo and group exhibitions by these artists over more than two decades, and periodically presents special projects and pop-up events in its space.

venues.name: Misa Shin Gallery
venues.about: Misa Shin Gallery opened in November 2010 in Shirokane, Tokyo, in a former ironworks building, and relocated in August 2018 to Minamiazabu, a quiet residential district near several embassies. The gallery presents exhibitions of Japanese and international artists working with a conceptual approach, giving particular attention to mid-career artists and to Japanese conceptualism of the 1960s and 1970s, aiming to reassess this postwar history for international audiences. Beyond its exhibition program, the gallery advises corporate art collections and art programs in Japan and has been involved in public art projects in Zhengzhou, China, and Doha, Qatar. It also explores connections between art and other disciplines such as architecture, theater and music.

venues.name: nca | nichido contemporary art
venues.about: nca | nichido contemporary art is a Tokyo gallery founded in 2002 as the contemporary branch of galerie nichido, itself established in 1928 as the first gallery in Japan to introduce Western painting. Building on that gallery's pioneering approach, nca focuses on introducing emerging Japanese and international artists working today. Since opening a branch in Taipei in 2015, the gallery has expanded its program to actively support and present contemporary art from across Asia, alongside artists from Europe and the Americas. The gallery is located in Roppongi, Tokyo, and participates regularly in international art fairs.

venues.name: CON_
venues.about: CON_ is a contemporary art gallery in Nihonbashi-Bakurocho, Tokyo, that opened in April 2022. It was founded by director Hisatomo Kato together with co-founders GILLOCHINDOX☆GILLOCHINDAE and Keiichi Toyama. The gallery's program deliberately crosses contemporary art with other expressive cultures, especially music, treating them as parts of a single organic movement within Tokyo's urban culture. Exhibitions and projects grow out of ongoing dialogue and research with artists, with the aim of building new contexts from contemporary experience rather than simply displaying finished work. Beyond its Tokyo space, CON_ regularly presents its artists through solo and group presentations at international art fairs across Asia, Europe and the United States.

venues.name: CLEAR GALLERY TOKYO / CLEAR EDITION INC
Base
venues.about: Base Gallery is a contemporary art gallery founded in 1986 in Tokyo, originally established as Matrix Japan S.A. It opened its first exhibition space in Ginza in 1988, moved to Kyobashi in 1995, and has been based in Kayabacho, in Tokyo's financial district, since 2004. The gallery mounts six to eight curated exhibitions a year and also runs an international art-dealing business spanning Japan, the Americas, Europe and Asia, handling modern and contemporary painting, sculpture and photography. It is particularly known for contemporary art from Southeast and East Asia. The gallery has also produced projects exploring the crossover of art and music, including the museum artegio in Yufuin, and operates a second space, Base Gallery Hakata, in Fukuoka.

venues.name: TALION GALLERY
venues.about: Talion Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo, founded in Yanaka in 2011 and relocated to Mejiro in 2014. Its name references the ancient principle of retributive justice, 'an eye for an eye,' reflecting the gallery's stated aim of generating new connections among the people, institutions, language and money that shape the contemporary art world. The gallery represents a small roster of Japanese artists working across painting, drawing, video and installation, and has participated in international art fairs including Art Düsseldorf, ART OSAKA, Art Fair Tokyo and the Seattle Art Fair, alongside museum and project-space collaborations in Japan and abroad.

venues.name: A Lighthouse called Kanata
venues.about: A Lighthouse called Kanata is a contemporary art gallery in the Jingumae area of Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, near Omotesando Station. It was established in 2007 by Wahei Aoyama with the aim of introducing contemporary Japanese art and aesthetics to an international audience. The gallery's program centers on sculpture and painting by artists working within an emerging strand of Japanese aesthetics that reinstates beauty, technique, and materiality as central concerns, spanning media such as ceramics, glass, lacquer, metal, bamboo and wood alongside painting. The gallery frames its mission around a 'Return to Innocence' in contemporary art practice, positioning its roster of artists, many working in traditional craft mediums, within a global contemporary art context.

venues.name: Gallery Tsubaki
venues.about: Gallery Tsubaki is a contemporary art gallery in the Kyobashi district of Tokyo, near Ginza. According to the gallery's own diary, its director left his father's gallery, Tsubaki Kindai Garou, to open Gallery Tsubaki around 1984. Since then it has built a program centered on Japanese artists working across painting, sculpture, ceramics, woodblock printmaking and photography, with a particular fondness for surreal, fantastical and meticulously crafted imagery. The gallery represents a large roster of emerging and mid-career Japanese artists, several of whom it has shown continuously for decades, and it regularly places their work in international art fairs across Taipei, Seoul, Busan and beyond, positioning itself as an advocate for Japanese contemporary art in the wider Asian market.

venues.name: Takuro Someya Contemporary Art
venues.about: Takuro Someya Contemporary Art (TSCA) is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Higashi-Shinagawa district, housed within the Terrada Art Complex. The gallery represents a small roster of Japanese and international artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, video and net-based media, including figures such as Kenjiro Okazaki, Rafaël Rozendaal, Mayumi Hosokura and Masaru Iwai. TSCA regularly mounts solo and group exhibitions in its Tokyo space and participates in major international art fairs, presenting its artists' work in dialogue with wider contemporary art discourse. The program spans generations, from established figures with museum retrospectives to younger practitioners exploring digital and performative practices.

venues.name: YOD Gallery Tennoz
venues.about: YOD Gallery is a contemporary art gallery based in Osaka, with an additional space in Tokyo. Its original space in Osaka's Shinmei Building opened in 2008 and closed in 2023 after fifteen years of exhibitions. The gallery's program has featured Japanese and international artists working in sculpture, ceramics, printmaking and installation, including an annual series called "Contiguous Zone" that introduces foreign artists' work in dialogue with Japanese sensibility. Exhibiting artists have included iron sculptor Takehito Fujii and printmaker/sculptor Masashi Hattori, alongside French artists such as Agathe de Bailliencourt, Catherine Gianola and Armel Barraud. The gallery has presented both solo and group shows exploring cross-cultural exchange and material-based practice.

venues.name: Mizuma Art Gallery (Ichigaya)
venues.about: Mizuma Art Gallery was founded in Tokyo in 1994 by Executive Director Sueo Mizuma. Since then it has built a program centered on Japanese and, increasingly, Southeast and East Asian artists whose work resists passing stylistic trends. The gallery expanded internationally, opening Mizuma Gallery in Singapore's Gillman Barracks in 2012, running the Rumah Kijang Mizuma residency in Yogyakarta from 2014 to 2019, and operating Mizuma & Kips in New York with Kips Gallery from 2018 to 2023. It regularly takes part in major international fairs such as Art Basel Hong Kong, Art Dubai and Art Taipei. In 2024 the gallery marked its thirtieth anniversary as a longstanding platform for contemporary art from diverse Asian backgrounds.

venues.name: Mizoe Art Gallery
venues.about: Mizoe Art Gallery was founded in Fukuoka in 2008 and opened a second space in Tokyo's Denenchofu neighborhood in 2012, linking the Kyushu and Tokyo art scenes and presenting Japanese art internationally. Both locations occupy detached houses set in large gardens in quiet residential areas; the Tokyo gallery is housed in a traditional Japanese-style residence where works are shown room by room. The gallery states its guiding concept as offering high-quality works and artists unaffected by trends or eras, favoring art of lasting, universal value. Its program spans modern and postwar Japanese painters and sculptors alongside major Western modern masters.

venues.name: The Tolman Collection
venues.about: The Tolman Collection is a Tokyo gallery specializing in contemporary Japanese prints, founded in 1972 by Norman and Mary Tolman. Often described as Japan's oldest foreign-owned gallery devoted to contemporary Japanese printmaking, it has built decades-long relationships with print artists, publishing exclusive editions and maintaining extensive archives. The gallery represents nearly fifty artists, working directly with them to ensure provenance and quality. Leadership passed to second-generation owner Allison Tolman, with Daisuke Maruoka serving as President. In addition to its Tokyo gallery, the collection operates a branch in New York. Over five decades it has organized exhibitions at institutions worldwide, including Zojoji Temple, the Singapore Art Museum, the Cairo Opera House, and Finland's Retretti Art Centre, helping introduce Japanese graphic art to international audiences.

venues.name: CANDYBAR Gallery
venues.about: CANDYBAR Gallery is a Kyoto gallery whose name evokes a compact, high-calorie snack bar, chosen to make art feel like an easy, everyday pleasure rather than something intimidating. The gallery's stated aim is to bring beauty into daily routines, encouraging visitors to enjoy 'lucky encounters' with art they love and to imagine the stories behind the works. It opened with a pre-opening sale period in August 2018. Located in the Ygion building near Gion in Higashiyama-ku, its artist roster spans both established Japanese and international postwar and contemporary names, alongside younger Japanese painters and printmakers shown in rotating exhibitions.

venues.name: YUKI-SIS
venues.about: YUKI-SIS is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Nihombashi Kayabacho district, currently directed by Yuki Terajima. The gallery's name blends the director's own name with the Egyptian goddess Isis. Before settling in Kayabacho in 2023, the gallery operated in other Tokyo neighborhoods linked by the word "bridge" (hashi), including Asakusabashi and near Nihombashi Mitsukoshimae. Its current space, on the second floor of the Koura Dai-Ichi Building overlooking a river and bridge leading to Tokyo Bay, sits among several other galleries in the same building. YUKI-SIS presents a program spanning painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, and animation, and participates in art fairs such as Art Fair Tokyo.

venues.name: YUKIKOMIZUTANI
venues.about: YUKIKOMIZUTANI is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo, founded in 2021 with the aim of bringing contemporary art from Tokyo to an international audience. The gallery is based inside TERRADA ART COMPLEX in Tennozu, an area where the Meguro River meets Tokyo Bay, home to the largest concentration of galleries in Japan. Through its exhibition program, YUKIKOMIZUTANI supports a diverse roster of artists working across painting, sculpture, textile and installation, and takes part in major art fairs in Japan and abroad. The gallery describes its mission as elevating the role of art in contemporary culture while helping develop Tennozu Isle into a significant arts and culture hub.

venues.name: AISHO
venues.about: AISHO is a Japanese gallery originally established in Hong Kong in 2012 as AISHONANZUKA, later renamed AISHO Hong Kong, with a Tokyo branch opening in 2024. Founded by Aisho Miura, the gallery is rooted in street art and focuses on introducing non-academic, non-mainstream creative talents to Asian and global audiences. Its program bridges diverse cultures and explores emerging markets across East Asia. AISHO represents a wide roster of international and Japanese artists, including figures such as Hajime Sorayama, Javier Calleja, Keiichi Tanaami, and Yoon Hyup, alongside street-art-oriented artists like Cyril Kongo and Joakim Ojanen. The gallery has participated in major international art fairs including the Armory Show, Art Basel Hong Kong, Miami, and Basel, and Frieze London.

venues.name: biscuit gallery
venues.about: biscuit gallery is a contemporary art gallery that opened in Shibuya, Tokyo in March 2021 before relocating to Shinjuku in June 2025. Alongside its Tokyo space it is preparing a second venue in Karuizawa, Nagano, due to open in summer 2026. The gallery represents a roster of emerging Japanese and Asian painters, photographers and mixed-media artists, and regularly presents them at international art fairs across Asia and Europe. Its program has included group and solo shows spanning painting, photography, sculpture and installation, often highlighting younger and Gen Z artists exploring identity, memory and material experimentation. Beyond its exhibition program, biscuit gallery runs an online shop, an art storage service, and 'grid next,' an open-call initiative supporting the discovery of new artists.

venues.name: GALLERY KTO (L'arte)
venues.about: GALLERY KTO is a contemporary art gallery based in Tokyo, with spaces in Shinjuku and Harajuku, founded in 2019. Under director Toshinori Tanaka, it has shown internationally recognized artists such as Jiro Takamatsu, Kenny Scharf and Bernd Koberling while increasingly supporting emerging and mid-career artists offering fresh perspectives. Though many represented artists work primarily in painting, the gallery also embraces sculpture, installation, photography and other interdisciplinary media. In recent years it has expanded beyond Japan through participation in international art fairs and collaborations, particularly in Asia, connecting Japanese artists with global audiences. Beyond its main spaces, the gallery organizes exhibitions across several Tokyo venues, presenting roughly forty shows a year.

venues.name: KOMIYAMA TOKYO G
venues.about: KOMIYAMA TOKYO G is a gallery space in Tokyo's Kanda-Jimbocho book district, launched in 2022 by the century-old secondhand bookstore Komiyama Shoten. It presents solo exhibitions and group shows spanning photography, illustration, ceramics, tattoo art, fashion and fetish culture, often mixing the bookstore's archival material with contemporary artists' work. Throughout the year it also hosts art book fairs and publication-related exhibitions tied to photobooks and artist monographs. The program favors emerging and cult-following artists working in painting, ceramics, digital/CG art, airbrush illustration, and documentary photography, reflecting the eclectic subcultural interests of its bookstore origins.

venues.name: space Un
venues.about: space Un is a Tokyo arts and culture venue focused on contemporary African art and cultural exchange between Japan and Africa. It was initiated by collector Edna Dumas, driven by her passion for contemporary African art and wish to support African artists, and co-founded with actor and artist Yuta Nakano. The gallery presents exhibitions of artists from the African continent and its diaspora, alongside cross-disciplinary programming including workshops, music events, film nights, and lectures. It also runs an invitation-only residency program linking artists' stays at Yoshino Cedar House in Nara with solo exhibitions in Tokyo. The gallery space in Minami-Aoyama was designed by architect Go Hasegawa, blending Japanese spatial sensibility with African heritage.

venues.name: Contemporary HEIS
venues.about: Contemporary HEIS is a Tokyo gallery founded in 2012 to specialize in contemporary art. It introduces young Japanese artists to audiences in Japan and abroad through exhibitions and international art fairs, while also mounting shows that revisit postwar Japanese movements such as Art Informel, Neo-Dada and Kyushu-ha. The gallery additionally deals in works by Mono-ha artists. Rather than confining itself to a single genre, Contemporary HEIS centers its program on abstract expression, building relationships with artists and collectors across a range of practices and generations.

venues.name: S.O.C Satoko Oe Contemporary
venues.about: Satoko Oe Contemporary (S.O.C.) is a contemporary art gallery in the Shirakawa district of Koto, Tokyo, which opened on 13 February 2016. The gallery represents a small roster of Japanese and international artists working across painting, sculpture, video and installation, including Takuya Ikezaki, Mitsuhiro Ikeda, Tadasuke Iwanaga, Teppei Kaneuji, Shinichiro Kano, Makiko Masutani, Chihiro Mori and Kesang Lamdark. Its exhibition program has also featured painters such as Shigeru Hasegawa and social-practice artist Yoshinori Niwa. The gallery has participated in art fairs abroad and joined with three other Tokyo galleries (Hagiwara Projects, Koki Arts and Maki Fine Arts) under the collective name Hammock for joint fair presentations.

venues.name: Shukado Gallery
venues.about: Gallery Shukado is a Ginza art dealership founded in 2003 (as Art Office JC, renamed Shukado Co., Ltd. in 2006), now led by second-generation president Chiaki Tanaka. Based in a seventh-floor space in Ginza 6-chome, Tokyo, it deals in Japanese art from the Edo period to today, including nihonga and Western-style painting, calligraphy, rare books and ukiyo-e, alongside appraisal, cataloguing and export services. In 2016 it launched SHUKADO CONTEMPORARY to promote younger artists, and in 2022 opened GALLERY SCENA in Harajuku for contemporary art. The gallery exhibits regularly at fairs in Japan and abroad.

venues.name: Canon Gallery S
venues.about: Canon Gallery Ginza is one of three Canon-run photography galleries in Japan, alongside spaces in Shinagawa and Osaka. It began in 1973 as the Canon Salon on Ginza 5-chome, offering a venue and support desk for professional photographers, and was renamed Canon Gallery Ginza in 2005 when it moved to its current Ginza 3-chome location. The space runs juried, open-submission exhibitions—open to professionals and amateurs alike—on roughly two-week rotations, with many shows later touring to Canon Gallery Osaka. It also hosts several company-curated exhibitions each year and sits adjacent to the Canon Photo House Ginza.

venues.name: Fuji Photo Gallery Ginza
venues.about: Fuji Photo Gallery Ginza is an exhibition space operated by CREATE, the professional photo lab founded in 1981 (as Photo Lab Create Tokyo) that has long supported photographers and photo enthusiasts through fine printmaking. Located since 2016 in the Success Ginza First Building near Ginza and Kyobashi stations, the gallery gives professional and amateur photographers alike a place to present silver-halide (gelatin silver) prints as finished works of art. The program emphasizes the tonal depth and craftsmanship of chromogenic printing, hosting both invited and open-call ('kobo') exhibitions. The gallery operates alongside CREATE's print production and framing services, positioning itself as a bridge between photographic creation and public presentation in central Tokyo.

venues.name: MISAKO & ROSEN
venues.about: Misako & Rosen is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Otsuka neighborhood, founded in 2006 by Misako Rosen and Jeffrey Rosen with a solo exhibition by Shimon Minamikawa. Since opening, the gallery has built a program centered on dialogue between Japanese and international artists, often through two-person and group exhibitions that pair local and overseas practices. Its roster spans painting, sculpture, photography and collaborative projects, and the gallery has developed long-running relationships with artists such as Shimon Minamikawa, Ken Kagami and Yui Yaegashi. Over nearly two decades it has expanded from local art fairs to a wide international fair circuit and collaborative projects with galleries abroad, while maintaining a small, artist-focused Tokyo space.

venues.name: Totem Pole Photo Gallery
venues.about: Totem Pole Photo Gallery is an artist-run photography space in Tokyo's Shinjuku ward, founded in 2008. It is operated collectively by twelve photographer-members who organize regular exhibitions of their own work alongside curated shows, events, workshops, and gallery rentals. Located on the first floor of the Dai-ni Fujikawa Building in Yotsuya, the gallery focuses on contemporary photographic practice, presenting a rotating program shaped by its member artists rather than a fixed roster of represented names outside the collective.

venues.name: Tomio Koyama Gallery Tennoz
venues.about: Tomio Koyama Gallery opened in 1996 in Saga-cho, Koto-ku, Tokyo, and has since become a key platform for Japanese contemporary art. From its earliest years the gallery took part in international art fairs and served as an early point of introduction for young Japanese artists, helping shape a broader current within the country's contemporary art scene. It now operates spaces in Roppongi, Tennoz, Maebashi, and, since November 2024, Kyobashi. The program spans generations and media, representing figures such as Kishio Suga, Hiroshi Sugito, Mika Ninagawa, and Richard Tuttle alongside exhibitions of ceramic artists, reflecting an approach that moves freely across nationality and genre.

venues.name: AWASE gallery
venues.about: AWASE gallery is a contemporary art gallery in Shinjuku, Tokyo, founded in 2025 by architect Riku Matsui and artist Kohei Yamada and based at the "nudge field" complex. Kohei Yamada curates the annual program, while Riku Matsui brings an architectural perspective, and the two develop exhibitions exploring the ambiguous theme of "Landscape." The program highlights artists and architects whose work engages with space and structure, spanning abstract painting, sculpture, and installation, with an emphasis on emerging talent from Japan and elsewhere in Asia. The gallery also runs a companion project space, On, in the same building, used for curated shows, cross-disciplinary collaborations, and rentable presentations for outside organizations.

venues.name: galerie a
venues.about: galerie a is a Tokyo project founded in 2020 by Nobuhiko Akiyoshi, a former buyer and wholesale agent who had worked for over a decade with domestic and international fashion designers before launching this gallery. Conceived during the COVID-19 pandemic, it operates as an online gallery that also stages physical, short-run exhibitions in Akiyoshi's own space, allowing visitors to experience works in person during limited open-gallery days. The program focuses on introducing Japan-based makers working by hand, spanning leather craft, textile sculpture, woodwork, and photography-informed leather goods, with an emphasis on artisans who pursue original, material-driven expression.

venues.name: KENJI TAKI GALLERY
venues.about: Kenji Taki Gallery is a contemporary art gallery with two spaces in Japan, one in Nagoya and one in the Roppongi district of Tokyo. The gallery's program centers on internationally recognized Japanese artists working across installation, sculpture, painting and photography, alongside select international names. Long associated with sculptor Isamu Wakabayashi (1936–2003), whose estate it continues to present, the gallery is also closely tied to Chiharu Shiota, known for large-scale thread and object installations exploring memory, life and death. Group presentations under a 'Gallery Artists' banner bring together a roster spanning several generations of Japanese contemporary practice, and the gallery participates in Japanese art fairs and maintains ongoing museum and biennale relationships for its artists.

venues.name: Design Festa Gallery
venues.about: Design Festa Gallery is a rental exhibition space in Harajuku, Tokyo, open to any artist regardless of experience or genre. Founded in spring 1998 on the concept of creating an open place for anyone expressing themselves, the gallery now spans two buildings, GALLERY WEST and GALLERY EAST, with over 70 spaces including more than 20 exhibition rooms of varying sizes and a Wall Paint Space for mural work. Exhibitions change daily, covering solo debuts, group shows, workshops, film screenings and product showcases. The gallery draws an average of over 300 visitors a day, about 30% of them from overseas, fostering direct interaction between exhibitors and the public. It is also used as a filming location and is affiliated with the biannual Design Festa art event.

venues.name: Gallery Le Déco
venues.about: LE DECO (Gallery Le Déco) is a multi-floor rental gallery space in Tokyo that hires out its rooms—spanning basement through several upper floors—to artists, apparel brands, and performers for exhibitions, trunk shows, and live events. Rather than representing artists or curating its own program, it functions as a venue-for-hire, providing floor space for paintings, photography, sculpture, and performance for periods of several days at a time. The gallery does not manage sales, take commission on works sold on-site, or provide invigilation, leaving oversight of artworks and events to the renters themselves.

venues.name: Ginza Graphic Gallery
venues.about: Ginza Graphic Gallery (ggg) is a gallery devoted to graphic design, established in March 1986 by Dai Nippon Printing Co. in Ginza, Tokyo, an area with a long history of art galleries and close to DNP's founding location. It is planned and operated by the DNP Foundation for Cultural Promotion, with supervision by Kaoru Kasai and Yoshihisa Tanaka. The gallery presents around eight exhibitions a year, inviting designers, artists and organizations from Japan and abroad, or working with collectors, and also runs lectures and publishes gggBooks. Its program focuses on graphic design history and contemporary practice, including posters, book design, and archival material.

venues.name: Shueisha Manga-Art Heritage Tokyo Gallery
venues.about: Shueisha Manga-Art Heritage (SMAH) is a project of the publisher Shueisha dedicated to presenting manga as fine art. Since 2008 the company has been digitally archiving original manga artwork, and it now produces limited-edition fine-art prints—using archival inkjet, letterpress, collotype and other rare printing techniques—supervised by the manga artists themselves. Each edition is registered on an art blockchain network to record provenance. SMAH operates a permanent gallery in Tokyo's Azabudai Hills, opened in 2023, and has presented its artists' work at art fairs and exhibitions in Kyoto, Miami and Venice. Its program focuses on iconic Japanese manga creators, from postwar pioneers to contemporary artists, treating their original drawings as museum-grade artworks.

venues.name: Espace Louis Vuitton Tokyo
venues.about: Espace Louis Vuitton Tokyo is a non-commercial exhibition space inaugurated in 2011, occupying a glass box on the top floor of the Louis Vuitton building in Omotesando, designed by Japanese architect Jun Aoki. Rather than a gallery representing artists for sale, it functions as an art space encouraging the creation of new contemporary artworks, staging rotating exhibitions by international contemporary artists such as Yayoi Kusama and Rina Banerjee. It is linked to a sister space, Espace Louis Vuitton Osaka, and to the Fondation Louis Vuitton, reflecting Louis Vuitton's broader engagement with contemporary art. Admission is free, and the program emphasizes striking architecture as much as the art displayed within it.

venues.name: Japanime Art Gallery Harajuku
venues.about: Japanime Art Gallery, operated by WAKON ARCS Inc., is dedicated to presenting original Japanese anime and manga production art—cels, genga, and production drawings—as fine art for an international audience. Rather than treating these works as mere by-products of animation, the gallery curates, preserves, and exhibits them as collectible artworks, aiming to build a recognized global market for anime art. The gallery is headquartered in Okinawa, Japan, with exhibition spaces in Harajuku and elsewhere in Tokyo, as well as Kyoto. Alongside exhibitions and sales, the company engages in curation, authentication, auction business, and cultural archive projects related to Japanese animation art.

venues-default.note: Gallery ranking defaults (rank_venues.py). Fair exhibitor lists and curated-list membership are the prestige priors; hours breadth is the client's 'bigger galleries are open more' signal; longevity/roster/cadence come from research reports (0 until research_venue.py runs). kind_museum is negative so museums rank as institutions, not galleries. require_verified is off until validate_venues.py has run for the city.

venues-la-ranked200.note: LA automatic gallery ranking refitted 2026-09-04 to the client's hand-ordered 'Los Angeles galleries' list (la-galleries-ranked.pdf, 200 entries; 148 gallery-kind entries rankable), top-weighted (nDCG gain 1/sqrt(list rank)). Only the curation-site knobs moved (weights + tiers); refs and list_weights are the 2026-09-03 top-100 fit. In-sample: 7/10 of the list's top 10 and 16/20 of its top 20 land in our top 10/20, P@50 .96, nDCG@20 .93 (live top-100 preset: 6/10, 14/20, .79). Remaining misses are data: Commonwealth and Council (#17, status unknown, no evidence), Marian Goodman (#9), Ghebaly (#11). The APPLIED LA ranking is the hand list itself via content/curation/los-angeles/venue_order.json; this preset is what 'Back to automatic ranking' falls back to.

venues-la-top100.note: LA gallery ranking fitted 2026-09-03 to the client's 'Los Angeles 100 Most Important Commercial Galleries' PDF (92 of 100 matched to the registry; 88 rankable). Differential-evolution fit of weights + list_weights + refs on graded nDCG@100 / P@100 / Spearman; 5-fold CV held-out AUC .93 vs .90 default. gates.kinds = gallery only (the PDF is commercial galleries; the site toggle turns it off). Fair/list multipliers encode prestige: Frieze LA / ABMB / ADAA members / Contemporary Art Daily high, GPLA membership ~0 (already counted by `directory`). Tiers = ranks 1-20 / 21-50 / 51-120 at fit time. kind_museum/kind_nonprofit only matter with the kinds gate off. Ceiling is data, not weights: ~28 list galleries had no fair/list/research evidence at fit time (research run launched the same day).
